name: Non-syndromic Pouch Colon
aliases: Congenital Pouch Colon without Syndromic Features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Pouch Colon

criteria.description: Presence of anorectal malformation with absent or malformed anal opening
Radiological or surgical identification of a shortened colon forming a pouch-like dilatation
No evidence of syndromic anomalies such as genitourinary or vertebral malformations
Contrast enema showing characteristic pouch colon morphology
Histopathology showing abnormal colonic musculature and mucosal changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anorectal malformation with pouch colon confirmed by imaging or surgery, and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing is not routinely diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to colonic pouch
searchTerms: swollen belly due to colon pouch

pathognomonic.symptomName: Meconium passage through fistula (e.g., genitourinary tract)
searchTerms: baby stool exiting via fistula to urinary tract
early stool passage through abnormal connection
throwing up due to intestinal obstruction

common.symptomName: Failure to pass meconium within 24-48 hours after birth
searchTerms: no stool passed within first two days
failure to pass first bowel movement

common.symptomName: Constipation or absence of bowel movements

occasional.symptomName: Urinary tract infection secondary to fistula
searchTerms: urinary infection caused by abnormal connection

occasional.symptomName: Mild respiratory distress due to abdominal distension
searchTerms: mild breathing difficulty from belly swelling
shortness of breath due to abdominal distension
respiratory distress caused by swollen abdomen

occasional.symptomName: Perineal excoriation from abnormal stool passage
searchTerms: skin irritation around anus from abnormal stool
perineal rash due to unusual stool passage
skin breakdown near anus from stool contact

occasional.symptomName: Mild electrolyte imbalance due to bowel dysfunction
searchTerms: mild imbalance of blood salts due to bowel issues
slight salt imbalance related to bowel problems

rare.symptomName: Hydronephrosis due to fistula-related urinary obstruction
searchTerms: urinary tract obstruction leading to kidney dilation
failure to thrive as a baby
poor weight gain in early life

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers if infection present
Electrolyte disturbances in severe bowel dysfunction
imaging: Contrast enema demonstrating shortened colon with pouch formation
Abdominal X-ray showing large gas shadow in lower abdomen
Ultrasound to assess associated genitourinary anomalies
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; non-syndromic presentation
other: Surgical findings of pouch colon with fistulous communication
Histopathology showing abnormal colonic muscle layer

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of associated syndromic anomalies such as vertebral or genitourinary malformations
Absence of ganglion cells in distal colon
Delayed passage of meconium without pouch colon morphology
Normal length colon without pouch formation

redFlags: Failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth
Severe abdominal distension with respiratory compromise
Signs of bowel perforation or sepsis
references: Gupta DK, Sharma S. Pouch colon syndrome: A unique regional variant of anorectal malformations. J Indian Assoc Pediatr Surg. 2010;15(3):83-89.
Saxena AK, Mathur P. Pouch colon syndrome: A clinico-pathological study. Pediatr Surg Int. 2000;16(5-6):383-386.
